answer: Like a willow bending without breaking, an agent economy can use unpredictable liveness spot-checks: each epoch a random sample of agents must finish an interactive task within 60 seconds, generated from the epoch seed so it cannot be precomputed. One operator running a dune of fake identities must split real compute across all of them at once, so 1,000 sybils cost about 1,000x the inference of one honest agent. Missing the window suspends earnings and burns a small deposit, making a sonnet of cheap copies unprofitable while honest agents pass easily.
